correctness.rationale: Tao gives the sum bound; reality gives conjugate pairing and nonnegativity gives strictly positive DC. On the p-point grid each midpoint cosine factor is nonnegative and zero exactly at its two closest samples. The possible last one-point factor is likewise nonnegative and has just the specified zero. The resulting p-k zeros use degree at most d=ceil((p-k)/2), and parity plus the sum bound forces the entire band [-d,d]. The positive multiplier preserves the zeros. At frequency d+s the unique contribution of order epsilon^s comes from the old coefficient at d with s positive frequency increments, giving the stated nonzero binomial leading term; no lower old frequency contributes at that order. Old coefficients persist by continuity and negative frequencies are conjugate. Degree D <= (p-1)/2 prevents aliasing. This includes k=p (constant starting function), k=1, zero multiplier exponent and p=3. Independent numerical replay checks 439 grid witnesses through p=23.
residual_risks: The finite replay uses floating-point thresholds; the universal claim rests on the proof.
No quantitative epsilon threshold or arbitrary prescribed support-set statement is proved.
